original_question:
Let ψ ∈ L2(R). For integers j,k ∈ Z, define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k). Call ψ a Parseval wavelet if ∑_{j,k∈Z} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|^2 = ||f||^2 for all f ∈ L2(R).

Is the collection of Parseval wavelets path connected in the L2(R) norm?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, the unnumbered Parseval-wavelet analogue of Problem 2.1 stated immediately after Conjecture 2.1.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended problem. It uses the correct ambient space L2(R), the correct classical one-dimensional dyadic translates and dilates ψ_{j,k}(x) = 2^{j/2}ψ(2^j x - k), the correct single-generator Parseval-frame condition Σ_{j,k∈Z} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|^2 = ||f||^2 for all f ∈ L2(R), and it asks exactly the right topological question: path connectedness in the L2(R)-norm topology. It also correctly avoids adding extra assumptions such as MRA, MSF, or spectral restrictions.
missing_details: State explicitly that this is the classical one-dimensional dyadic setting of Section 2: integer translates and dyadic dilations only.
Define the class under study as the full set of all single-generator Parseval wavelets W_P ⊂ L2(R), not a special subclass such as MRA Parseval wavelets or MSF Parseval wavelets.
Spell out path connectedness in subset form: for any ψ0, ψ1 ∈ W_P, there should exist a norm-continuous path Ψ : [0,1] → L2(R) with Ψ(0)=ψ0, Ψ(1)=ψ1, and Ψ(t) ∈ W_P for every t ∈ [0,1].
Note that in the paper this is not given as a separately numbered open problem; it is presented as the Parseval-wavelet variant of Problem 2.1 immediately after Conjecture 2.1.
Make explicit that no additional hypotheses on the Fourier support or multiresolution structure are intended; those appear only as known special connected subclasses in the surrounding discussion.
refined_question: In the classical one-dimensional dyadic setting, let W_P := {ψ ∈ L2(R) : the system {ψ_{j,k}(x) = 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x - k)}_{j,k∈Z} is a Parseval frame for L2(R), equivalently Σ_{j,k∈Z} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|^2 = ||f||^2 for every f ∈ L2(R)}. Is W_P path connected in the L2(R)-norm topology? Equivalently, for any ψ0, ψ1 ∈ W_P, does there exist a continuous map Ψ : [0,1] → L2(R) such that Ψ(0)=ψ0, Ψ(1)=ψ1, and Ψ(t) ∈ W_P for all t ∈ [0,1]?
justification: The nearest official target is not Conjecture 2.1 itself, because Conjecture 2.1 concerns orthonormal wavelets with a fixed wavelet dimension function. Your draft instead matches the immediately following, unnumbered Parseval-wavelet variant of Problem 2.1 in Section 2.1: the paper first states the general orthonormal connectivity problem in the one-dimensional dyadic setting, then defines Parseval wavelets in that same setting and says that the corresponding connectivity problem remains open in full generality. The surrounding paragraph also records only partial positive results for special Parseval subclasses, which confirms that the intended question is the unrestricted path-connectedness problem for all dyadic Parseval wavelets.

citations.label: Unnumbered paragraph immediately following Conjecture 2.1 (definition of Parseval wavelet; statement that the problem remains open in full generality; partial results for MRA and spectral subclasses)
